verdict.reasoning: Headaches are frontal and mostly at work: patient says headaches are ‘mostly in the front’ and ‘I get it, mostly when I'm, at work.’

Palpitations: ‘you mentioned that you noticed your heart beating’ with frequency described later. SOB at desk: ‘do you feel short of breath while you're sitting at your desk?’ Patient: ‘Yes.’ Bilateral hand tingling: ‘Is it in one hand? Or both hands?’ Patient: ‘Both.’ Decreased appetite: ‘you also mentioned your reduced appetite. So, you don't want to eat as much.’ 5‑pound unintentional weight loss: ‘Can you remember how much you've lost?’ Patient: ‘Five pounds.’ and ‘It's not intentional, no.’ Decreased libido: ‘I do have like, some loss of libido at home.’

Temporal relation to job change: ‘it started roughly when I changed jobs.’ Occurs at work during meetings or laptop use: ‘Not really. I get it, mostly when I'm, at work… I'm in a meeting, or on my laptop.’
Patient describes mild nausea: ‘do you feel sick?’ Patient: ‘not, not, not really… I kind of feel a little bit nauseous maybe.’
No headaches on commute: ‘So, do you get these headaches on your commute in to work?’ Patient: ‘Not really. I get it, mostly when I'm, at work.’
SOB not with exercise: ‘So, do you feel short of breath while you're sitting at your desk?’ Patient: ‘Yes.’ Then, ‘And, how about when you're exercising?’ Patient: ‘No.’
Approximate daily palpitations: ‘how often do you get that?’ Patient: ‘it's maybe once a day, uh, maybe more.’

Transcript notes tingling in arms and both hands, and mentions elevator in context of fast heart beating: ‘I just sometimes also get like some, tingling in my arms… especially… when I, come into the elevator… my heart is beating, kinda fast.’ There is no explicit statement that bilateral hand tingling specifically occurs in the elevator.
No prior headache history: ‘And, do you normally get headaches, before all of this started?’ Patient: ‘No, I, I feel like my… health situation was mostly under control.’
‘Do you have any other medical problems?’ Patient: ‘well I have, hyperthyroidism.’
Medication and adherence: ‘do you take medications for that?’ Patient: ‘Thyroxine.’… ‘are you remembering to take your medications?’ Patient: ‘Yes.’
Alcohol use: ‘How much do you drink?’ Patient: ‘Like, once a week, couple of glasses, of wine.’

No smoking or recreational drugs: ‘And, how about smoking?’ Patient: ‘No.’… ‘do you do anything else recreational, in terms of drugs?’ Patient: ‘No.’… ‘So, you've never taken cocaine, or marijuana?’ Patient: ‘No.’

Recurrent frontal headaches: ‘mostly in the front.’ Associated with work and mild nausea and started after job change: ‘it started roughly when I changed jobs… mostly when I'm, at work… I kind of feel a little bit nauseous maybe.’
Palpitations and SOB at rest/desk and not on exertion: SOB at desk ‘Yes’; with exercise ‘No’; palpitations are described in non‑exertional context and frequency ‘maybe once a day.’

Intermittent bilateral hand paresthesias are supported (‘Is it in one hand? Or both hands?’ Patient: ‘Both.’), but the transcript links the elevator scene to arm tingling and fast heart beat, not clearly to hand paresthesias specifically.

Decreased appetite: ‘you also mentioned your reduced appetite.’ 5‑pound unintentional weight loss: ‘Five pounds… It's not intentional, no.’ Decreased libido: ‘I do have like, some loss of libido at home.’
Past medical history and management: ‘well I have, hyperthyroidism.’… ‘do you take medications for that?’ ‘Thyroxine.’
In‑person appointment: ‘I think the best course of action is, you come and see, one of our doctors, in the clinic.’ and ‘we're going to do is book an appointment… to come and see us clinic.’
Focus on cardiovascular and respiratory exam: ‘We can give you an examination, and what that means is, we check your heart and your breathing.’
Blood tests for thyroxine: ‘And probably do some blood tests, for your thyroxine.’
Deferring new medications: ‘I think before we give you any medications, we should see you in person.’
